history.summary: Kali temple at Kathalbari (LNMU campus area), Darbhanga, built by Maharaja Kameshwar Singh in 1933 on the funeral pyre (samadhi/crematorium ghat) of his father Maharaja Rameshwar Singh - an unusual temple built atop a pyre. Named Rameshwari Shyama Mai after the king. Nagara-style architecture. The sanctum holds a huge idol of Maa Kali beside Mahakal, with Ganapati and Batukabhairava to the left; the Mund Mala around the goddess's neck is said to depict the letters of the Hindi alphabet, symbolising creation. Both Vedic and Tantric rituals are performed here - uncommon for one temple; the temple aarti has special significance and devotees wait for hours to join it. Weddings and other manglik (auspicious) ceremonies are performed here despite the pyre location. Large crowds and a fair during Navratri.

name: Shyama Kali Temple (Shyama Mai / Rameshwari Kali Temple)
town_description: Darbhanga is a historic city in the Mithila region of north Bihar, long the seat of the Darbhanga Raj - one of the largest and most cultured zamindaris of British India. Known for its royal palaces (Rambagh, Darbhanga Fort/Raj Qila), the Chandradhari Museum, and Maithil art, language and cuisine, it is the cultural capital of Mithila.
